idiom_name: throw at the boundary + never-based exhaustiveness checking (compile-time fail-fast)
implementation_notes: TypeScript keeps the JavaScript throw and adds a compile-time half: narrowing a discriminated union to never makes any unhandled case a type error, so an exhaustive switch with const _check: never = value refuses stale code at build time instead of at runtime - the type system performing the fail-fast check. Runtime guards are written as explicit TypeError/domain-error throws at the boundary, or as assertion functions (asserts value is T) that document the check in the signature; both replace any need for a hand-rolled validation framework as long as the data is already typed. Untrusted input from the edge is the exception: it must be parsed and validated, because types are erased at runtime.
pitfalls: Types are erased at runtime: a narrow type annotation on a network payload is not validation, so fail-fast guards must run before the value is trusted.
Swallowing converts the failure back into a default - .catch(() => undefined) or an empty catch block keeps the code compiling while removing the fail-fast path.
Synchronous throw inside a callback whose API ignores errors (setTimeout, event handlers, non-awaited async functions) becomes an unhandled rejection; guards must sit inside the awaited boundary.
